from journal.repositories.id_blocks import IdBlocks
from journal.repositories.shared_tables import SharedTables
from journal.sync.team_server_link import TeamServerLink


class BlockSupply:
    """The row numbers this machine asks the team server for: a new block for each shared table running low."""

    def __init__(self, link: TeamServerLink, blocks: IdBlocks, tables: SharedTables) -> None:
        self.link, self.blocks, self.tables = link, blocks, tables

    def refill(self) -> None:
        wanted = [table for table in self.tables.names() if self.blocks.is_wanted(table)]
        if wanted:
            for grant in self.link.fetch_blocks(wanted).blocks:
                self.blocks.add(grant.row_table, grant.first, grant.last)
EOF

from pathlib import Path
Path("src/journal/version.py").write_text('VERSION = "4.28.0"\n')
lines = [
 "- Joining a team never renames an environment on your machine. Each environment has a random key, made with it and never changed, and that key is how your machine and the team server match it. Its name stays your own; the team knows it under your name before it, as project-main. A colleague's environment arrives under that team name.",
 "- A journal that runs out of row numbers from the team server asks it for more there and then, and if the server cannot be reached it no longer holds every tool call.",
]
p = Path("src/journal/CHANGELOG.md"); s = p.read_text()
s = s.replace("## 4.27.1\n", "## 4.28.0\n\n" + "\n".join(lines) + "\n\n## 4.27.1\n", 1)
p.write_text(s)
Path("/EXAMPLE-KEY.28.0.md").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
p = Path("NOTES.md"); s = p.read_text()
anchor = "## The shared journal\n"
assert anchor in s
s = s.replace(anchor, anchor + """
- **Environments are matched by key, never renamed (task 1558, 2026-10-23, Sir project's word).** An environment
  carries a random key, made with it and never changed, uniquely indexed. Its `name` is a local field
  (`Model.local_fields`): it never leaves the machine, so joining a team changes no name on this machine and moves no
  worktree. Its `team_name`, the owner's prefix before the name, is what the team server and other machines know; a
  pulled environment takes its team name as its local name. A join's download re-owns this machine's environments by
  key, or makes them anew under their team names. The rename this replaced left a joined journal unable to find the
  environment its running agent had started in.
""", 1)
p.write_text(s)
EOF
echo ok

sub("CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 3600\n", "")
sub("asked of GitHub at most hourly on a thread of its own, on a shared journal only the version the team is pinned to, and its install: on its own when the user has switched that on, when they say so, or on a hosted journal as soon as the team is pinned to another version, which it never upgrades the team to itself.",
    "asked of GitHub as often as the settings say on a thread of its own, on a shared journal only the version the team is pinned to, and its install: on its own when the user has switched that on, when they say so, or on a hosted journal as soon as the team is pinned to another version; a hosted journal with the auto-update on is the team's own and installs each newer release, pinning the team to it.")
sub("account: TeamAccount, client: SyncClient, hosting: Hosting) -> None:\n        self.account, self.client, self.hosting = account, client, hosting\n",
    "account: TeamAccount, client: SyncClient, hosting: Hosting, link: TeamServerLink) -> None:\n        self.account, self.client, self.hosting, self.link = account, client, hosting, link\n")
sub("        self._checked_at = timing.time() - CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS + FIRST_CHECK_DELAY_SECONDS\n", "        self._next_check_at = timing.time() + FIRST_CHECK_DELAY_SECONDS\n")
sub("release.upgrades(self.running()) and self.account.allows(release)]", "release.upgrades(self.running()) and (self.leads_team() or self.account.allows(release))]")
sub("""    def is_hosted(self) -> bool:
        return self.hosting.is_hosted()
""", """    def is_hosted(self) -> bool:
        return self.hosting.is_hosted()

    def leads_team(self) -> bool:
        from journal.features.updates.feature import Updates
        return self.is_hosted() and bool(self.settings.option(Updates.AUTO)) and not self.branch()

    def check_interval_seconds(self) -> int:
        from journal.features.updates.feature import Updates
        return self.settings.integer(Updates.CHECK_INTERVAL) * 60
""")
sub("""        elif time - self._checked_at >= CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS:
            self._checked_at = time
""", """        elif time >= self._next_check_at:
            self._next_check_at = time + self.check_interval_seconds()
""")
sub("""    def checked(self) -> None:
        self.read()
""", """    def checked(self) -> None:
        self.lead(VERSION)
        self.read()
""")
sub("""        self.problem = ""
        self.card.step("Restarting the journal")
""", """        self.problem = ""
        self.lead(target.label)
        self.card.step("Restarting the journal")
""")
sub("""    def restart(self) -> None:""", """    def lead(self, version: str) -> None:
        if not self.leads_team() or not self.account.is_joined():
            return
        if not any(Release(version).is_newer(pinned) for pinned in Release.lookup([self.account.team_version()])):
            return
        try:
            self.link.pin_version(version)
        except (OSError, TeamRefusal) as refused:
            self.problem = f"The team could not be pinned to {version}: {refused}"

    def restart(self) -> None:""")
p.write_text(t)

EOF

command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
from pathlib import Path
p = Path("NOTES.md")
lines = p.read_text().split("\n")
i = next(n for n, l in enumerate(lines) if l.startswith("- **The hosted journal follows the team's pinned version (task 1538).**"))
lines.insert(i + 1, "- **The hosted journal leads the team's version when its auto-update is on (task 1557).** The setting updates.check_minutes (default 60) sets how often the updater asks GitHub; the team image's hosted.sh turns updates.auto on and sets the check to one minute at the hosted journal's first start. A hosted journal with updates.auto on and no branch followed is offered every newer release of its major version, not only the pinned one, installs it and pins the team to it before it restarts, and pins the team to its own version at each check while the team is behind it, so a failed pin is tried again. The team server lets its relay account pin the version as an admin may. With updates.auto off it follows the admin's pin as before.")
p.write_text("\n".join(lines))
p = Path("src/journal/version.py")
p.write_text(p.read_text().replace('"4.28.1"', '"4.29.0"'))
note = "- The journal checks for a new release as often as you set it to, on the Settings page beside the auto-update switch, every 60 minutes by default.\n- A team's hosted journal installs each new release on its own and moves the team to it, checking every minute; every member's status bar then asks to install it."
p = Path("src/journal/CHANGELOG.md")
p.write_text(p.read_text().replace("## 4.28.1\n", f"## 4.29.0\n\n{note}\n\n## 4.28.1\n", 1))
Path("/EXAMPLE-KEY.29.0.md").write_text(note + "\n")
EOF
journal await "the full suite" --output 13587

command: journal task edit 1568 --title "Every chat row is a typed message of the chat's own agent, else it is refused" --brief "Messages 29513 and 29517: Mr. Muybridge's (worker 57) seventeen search cards showed in the main chat as if the main agent's. Fix it at the source, as the user set out: everything the chat shows is a chat message; every chat message must name its type and the agent it belongs to, and the messages repository refuses to store one that names no type, or whose agent is not the agent of the chat it is written to. The chat is then scoped by that agent id, so nothing from a worker, a subagent or anything else reaches it unless it is of that agent. Done when a test saves a message with no type and one from a worker into the main chat and both are refused, a worker's search no longer shows in the main chat, and a screenshot shows the chat clean."

command:
cat > /tmp/muy/strip.py <<'EOF'
import sys
from PIL import Image
# a strip of crops: out, box "l,t,r,b", then the screenshots in order, each scaled up `scale` times
out, box, scale, *srcs = sys.argv[1:]
box = tuple(int(v) for v in box.split(","))
scale = int(scale)
crops = [Image.open(s).crop(box) for s in srcs]
w, h = crops[0].size
sheet = Image.new("RGB", (len(crops) * (w * scale + 6), h * scale), (255, 255, 255))
for i, c in enumerate(crops):
    sheet.paste(c.resize((w * scale, h * scale), Image.LANCZOS), (i * (w * scale + 6), 0))
sheet.save(out)
EOF

If bars dock while a figure is mid-fall, it can fall past the compose top to the window's foot; I only saw that because my faked dock flickered, and the fall rules are unchanged. The server's voice catalogue was not touched." 2>&1 | tail -1
